title: Norfolk OPP cleared in Delhi man's death;
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has absolved police of any wrongdoing in the death of a Delhi man who was Tasered four times.
In a statement released Wednesday, the SIU said Jeffrey Mark Marreel, 36, died last year of acute cocaine poisoning.
Marreel's death will be the subject a coroner's inquest, which has yet to be scheduled.
Norfolk OPP arrested Marreel last June 23 in Fisher's Glen following reports of a man acting erratically.
In an unusually detailed report on the incident, the SIU said Marreel posed a danger to himself and others.
Three officers were needed to subdue Marreel and take him into custody.
After he was taken to OPP headquarters in Simcoe, Marreel showed signs of "medical distress."
He was taken to Simcoe's Norfolk General Hospital, where he died.
Four SIU investigators and two forensic investigators probed Marreel's death.
SIU director Ian Scott said officers had reason to arrest Marreel on a number of grounds, including causing a disturbance, uttering threats and assault with a weapon.
He added that the police use of force was reasonable.

"The evidence collected by the SIU, in my view, establishes that the officers' use of force fell within the latitude authorized by the criminal law as being no more than was reasonably necessary to overcome Mr. Marreel's violence and effect his arrest," Scott said in a statement.
Frank Phillips, spokeman for the SIU, said Wednesday that police discharged the stun function of their Taser devices four times.
Phillips would not share the duration of these jolts or how closely together they were administered.
"That information will be part of the inquest," Phillips said.
"It would not be appropriate for me to release that at this time."
Last month, the SIU suggested it would not publicize details of its investigation for legal reasons.
This drew criticism from Peter Hellyer, chairman of the Norfolk police services board, and members of the Marreel family, who said the SIU had kept them in the dark about their son's investigation.
Phillips said Wednesday that the Marreel family was told of the SIU's findings before they were released.
Noel Marreel, Jeffrey Marreel's father, would not comment last month on the possibility of a lawsuit.
He also had no comment Wednesday.
"My lawyer told me not to say anything," Marreel said.
The SIU said Marreel was brandishing a metal step when police arrived in Fisher's Glen.
The first officer on the scene said he was threatened physically and verbally.
The officer remained in the cruiser awaiting reinforcements.
The SIU said Marreel threw a piece of metal at the cruiser.
As well, "Mr. Marreel harm himself and damage various objects in the area, including trees, a stop sign and a telephone junction box."
After two more officers arrived, officers decided to try to arrest Marreel.
He was ordered to drop the stop and get down on the ground.
"Mr. Marreel dropped the step.
Mr. Marreel was again ordered to lie face down on the ground.
Mr. Marreel did not do so.
A struggle ensued as the officers reached Mr. Marreel and force was used by the officers to eventually subdue him and handcuff him," the SIU said.
The SIU is a civilian agency which investigates when people are injured or killed while interacting with police.
